name: arc-pattern-horizontal-mirror-into-zero-rectangle
description: Use when ARC shows a colored motif and a same-sized zero rectangle. Copy the motif into the zero rectangle, mirrored left-to-right.
---

# Mirror motif into zero rectangle

When an ARC grid contains a compact, non-background colored motif and a separate rectangular block of zeros, check whether the zero block matches the motif's bounding-box dimensions. If so, a recurring rule may be to place a left-to-right horizontal reflection of the motif into that block while leaving all other cells unchanged.

## Procedure
1. Identify the motif's exact bounding box and the zero rectangle's location/dimensions.
2. Verify dimensions match; retain background cells outside the motif if the source box includes any.
3. Reflect each motif row horizontally (reverse the columns within the motif's bounding box); do not rotate or vertically flip.
4. Replace the zeros with the reflected motif; preserve the rest of the grid.
5. Validate output dimensions and every row width before submitting.

## Recurrence evidence: task-6c30b7cd
A 12x12 input had a 3x4 motif at rows 1–3, columns 1–4:
`1112 / 1121 / 1222`, with a separate 3x4 zero rectangle at rows 9–11, columns 2–5. The accepted output placed the row-wise horizontal reflection there:
`2111 / 1211 / 2221`.
A demonstration independently confirmed this: its 4x4 source motif and 4x4 zero block matched, and the output block was the source reflected left-to-right. This task-specific transformation was accepted on the first submission with one demonstration request. Treat this as a hypothesis to test, not a universal rule; use demos when dimensions or orientation remain ambiguous."
}
